title: Ham-and-Cheese Brioche Pudding or Strada
description: Bread pudding, an old-fashioned frugal dessert, usually contains day-old bread, milk, eggs and a bit of fruit, fresh or dried, baked in a sweet custard. This savory version, made with ham and cheese, employs tender buttery brioche. It is easier to make than a quiche, but has a similar delicacy, perfect for lunch or a light supper.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon butter, for greasing the pan
1 (12-ounce) brioche loaf or smaller brioches or maybe croissants, cut into 1-inch cubes (about 8 cups)
6 ounces sliced ham, (or maybe something interesting like thick cut prosciutto, or pancetta, Canadian bacon, or even regular bacon or sausage), cut crosswise into matchsticks (about 1 1/2 cups)
8 ounces grated Gouda or Gruyère or Emmenthaler cheese (about 4 cups)
directions: Heat oven to 375 degrees. Butter an 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Fill dish with brioche cubes and set aside.
In a large bowl, beat eggs well. Whisk in half-and-half, salt, pepper, nutmeg, cayenne, mustard, and scallions. Pour mixture over cubes in baking dish.
Sprinkle ham and cheese on top of mixture and press down to make sure everything is submerged. Set baking dish on a rimmed baking sheet.

Transfer baking dish and baking sheet to the middle shelf of the oven, and bake for 45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted in the middle of the dish emerges dry. Let rest for 10 minutes or so before serving.
notes:
Tip:
If desired, let pudding cool completely and cut into squares or wedges. Then reheat for 10 minutes at 375 degrees.
